discover_page.text: Tisno lies where the island of Murter almost touches the mainland, separated by a strait just 40 meters wide. Today it's the administrative center of a municipality rich in history. From Roman ruins and an 11th-century church to the 18th-century sanctuary on Brošćica hill. With its long waterfront, lush greenery, and nearby beaches, Tisno invites you to stroll, relax, and savor homemade Dalmatian flavors from the surrounding countryside.

sibenik.title: Šibenik
sibenik.text: Šibenik, the oldest self-governing Croatian city on the Adriatic, is located in the most protected natural harbor, in the central part of the Adriatic Sea's eastern coast, at the mouth of the Krka River, likely at the place where some of the first settled Croats first saw the sea.

zadar.title: Zadar
zadar.text: The history of Zadar dates back three thousand years when it was mentioned as a settlement, while the urbanized area has existed for two thousand years. Since then, Zadar has been one of the most important cities on the eastern Adriatic and an essential destination for adventurers, poets, and writers. Its streets, squares, waterfront, churches, and monumental heritage reveal this ancientness at every turn, while modern installations are a vision of contemporary life and an inspiration for new travelers. Three thousand years ago, the foundations were laid, and the adventure had already begun.

krka.title: Krka National Park
krka.text: The National Park is a vast, predominantly unaltered area of exceptional and multiple natural values, encompassing one or more preserved or slightly altered ecosystems. Its purpose is primarily scientific, cultural, educational, and recreational, and due to visitors, there are also tourist activities. With its submerged part at the mouth, the Krka River is about 72.5 km long and is the 22nd longest river in Croatia. It springs from the foot of the Dinara mountain, 3.5 km northeast of Knin. With seven travertine waterfalls and a total drop of 224 m, Krka is a natural and karst phenomenon. The travertine waterfalls of the Krka River are a fundamental phenomenon of this river.

kornati.title: Kornati National Park
kornati.text: The Kornati National Park is a unique archipelago consisting of 89 islands, islets, and reefs, located in the central part of the Adriatic Sea. It is known for its stunning natural beauty, crystal-clear waters, and rich biodiversity. The park offers a variety of activities for visitors, including sailing, diving, and exploring the islands' historical and cultural heritage.
